Review of afea882 (1.24.37: a transistor's line that names a part no line has, AI_ELECTRONICS circuit() and build())
Reviewer: a separate agent that did not write the change. Run 2026-11-24.

WHAT WAS RUN
  node tests/fixtures/review_electronics_1237/replay.js <afea882's src/lantern.inner.html>   -> run_afea882.txt
  204 cases: 153 AGREE, 51 DISAGREE (20 high, 21 medium, 10 low)
  - 184 cases of my own (cases.js): replies as the 35B and the small models write them, in questions about relays,
    motors, fans, pumps, lamps, bulbs, solenoids, buzzers, beepers, LEDs, push buttons, ESP32 at 3.3 V, two
    transistors, lowercase tags, MAKE SCHEMATIC blocks, the guide's own lines, IDs like MOT1, M10, M01, KA1, RL1.
  - 20 guard cases: every saved reply in tests/fixtures/bench_run*.json with a block read as electronics (harvest.js,
    guard.js), built on afea882 and compared with 22b1c03 (guard_before.json): ok, problems, branches, summary.
  - The same run on the working tree's HEAD (a7548cd, which changes only the notes' ANS) gives the same 204 lines.
  - Run on 22b1c03 itself: 130 AGREE, 74 DISAGREE (the 35B's two tries and the other new readings go back there).
  Not run: npm test, the browser tests, any model. Everything here is Lantern's reading of replies I wrote or that
  the bench saved; nothing was tried on the 35B or the small models.

WHAT AGREES
  - The laptop's two tries (bench set B, the motor question) now draw as meant: Q1 switching M1 from P1, the
    model's own D1 across M1, and what was read is said ("Q1's line names K1, which no line has: M1 is the one
    motor ..."; "Lantern added motor M1, which Q1's line names"). The bench grades both a pass. Also in lowercase,
    and in a MAKE SCHEMATIC block.
  - A lone transistor line whose part is the question's one load kind is drawn right: relay, motor, fan ("a small
    fan", "a cooling fan"), "a DC motor", "a 12 V pump motor", lamp, "light bulb", solenoid, buzzer, "beeper";
    on an ESP32 pin (3.3 V kept); two transistors each with their own part; a push button driving the base.
  - The free-load reading is right where the block has one load of the asked kind on Q1's pin or none: RL1,
    BC547, D9 (the board's name for the pin), the guide's K1 beside the model's own motor (the 0.8B's way).
    It stays back where it should: the load on another pin, two free loads, a pin line naming the load.
  - All 56 "same" cases build exactly as on 22b1c03 (ok, problems, branches, summary): right replies of every kind
    above, part / wire schematics, the guide copied whole, and replies with no unknown part or no load word.
  - The prompts are unchanged: aiAct.prompt and the tools offered for all 300 bench questions, and
    AI_ELECTRONICS PROMPT and HINT.
  - Saved replies: of 20, 12 build exactly as before; the 35B's 2 now draw (right); 2 (the 0.8B's empty blocks in
    the relay question) now get "add the relay the question asks for, like: relay K1" (better); 4 get another pin
    line (below).

HIGH (20 cases, two causes)

H1. The part is added even when the block already has a load of that kind under another tag, or a load no
    transistor switches. Two loads are drawn, the declared one wired straight across the supply (always on), or
    given a second transistor on the same pin. On 22b1c03 every one of these went back with the right line
    ("transistor Q1 M1 P1", "transistor Q1 KA1 P1", ...). Rule 7: "M2 could be the M1 the block declares" is an
    answer to "what else can it be", so it is not sure.
      typo-M2-for-M1     motor M1 "12 V" + transistor Q1 M2 P1 -> "M1 (12 V) runs. P1 high turns Q1 on: M2 runs"
      relay-RL1-guide-line  relay RL1 "12 V coil" + the guide's "transistor Q1 K1 P1" (the 35B's first try, in the
                         relay question) -> "RL1 (12 V coil) pulls in" always, plus an added relay K1
      relay-RLY1-guide-line, relay-KA1, relay-K2-for-K1, motor-MOT1, fan-F1, fan-FAN1-M1, typo-M10, bulb-B1,
                         lamp-LP1, solenoid-SOL1: the same, for each kind and tag style
      motor-on-pin-M2, relay-on-pin-K2, motor-MOT1-on-pin-M1, buzzer-BZ2: the declared load is on Q1's own pin;
                         it gets an added Q2 (or drives directly), and a second load is added for Q1 -- two motors and
                         two transistors on P1
      two-motors-one-typo, led-and-motor-typo: a third motor added, M2 / M1 always on
      motor-question-relay-chosen: "switch a 230 V motor through an NPN transistor"; the model drew a 5 V relay K1
                         and wrote "transistor Q1 M1 P1" with a note that K1's contacts run the motor. Drawn: K1
                         always on, and a motor M1 on the 5 V rail switched by Q1.
    The bench's own check would fail typo-M2-for-M1 (its first motor branch has no transistor), so a run would show
    these only as a lost point, not as what was drawn.

H2. The part is added to a transistor whose line already names a declared load. Q1 then switches two loads, the
    wire walk fails, and the model is sent "Lantern could not draw this circuit correctly (Q1 does not switch M1's
    lower end to 0 V)" -- no line to write (rule 3).
      two-refs-relay-and-motor-contact: "switch a 24 V DC motor through an NPN transistor"; relay K1 "24 V coil",
      transistor Q1 K1 M1 P1, note K1's contacts run the motor M1. 22b1c03 drew Q1 switching K1 (what the reply
      means); afea882 sends the walk's failure. Also two-refs-relay-question-motor, two-refs-led-and-motor,
      two-refs-solenoid-known (medium: what 22b1c03 drew there was not clearly right either).

    A mend that would pass every case here: add the part only when Q1's line names no declared load AND no load in
    the block is left unswitched; otherwise fall to the free-load reading (which already wants exactly one free load
    of the asked kind, on Q1's pin or none), and when that is not sure, go back as 22b1c03 did, with the line naming
    the free load ("transistor Q1 RL1 P1"). Not tried.

MEDIUM (21)

M1. exId is the block's first load of any kind. In a relay or motor question with an LED declared first, every
    line handed back names the LED: "transistor Q1 switches nothing ... like: transistor Q1 D1 P1" (as before) and
    now the pin line too, which said "transistor Q1 K1 P1" on 22b1c03. Copied, Q1 switches the LED and the relay
    together and the LED's own pin goes back again.
      back-switches-nothing-led-first (+ -copy), free-led-and-motor-line (+ -copy), free-only-led-in-relay-question,
      guard bench_run_1247_08b/make-electronics/first ("(transistor Q1 D1 P3)" in the relay question; was K1)
    The first load of the asked kind, else one[2] + "1", would name the right part.

M2. A pin that drives nothing now gets only "transistor Q1 <exId> <pin>" whenever the question names a load kind.
    Lost: "led D1 Pn" and "switch S1 Pn", which an LED + relay or button + relay question needs; and the transistor
    named is Q1 even when Q1 already switches that load from another pin (copied, Q1 gets a second pin and the same
    problem comes back).
      back-pin-led-relay (P2 is the LED's: told "transistor Q1 K1 P2"), back-pin-button-relay ("D2 input": told
      "transistor Q1 K1 P1"), back-pin-two-motors (+ -copy: told "transistor Q1 M1 P2"; the line for this question is
      "transistor Q2 M2 P2"), back-led-question-fan-word (an LED question that names a fan: told "transistor Q1 D1 P2")

M3. "there is nothing to power or read: add the motor ..., like: motor M1 (with transistor Q1 M1 P1)" writes P1 even
    when the reply's pin is P3, beside two other problems that say P3. Copied, a pin P1 is added and P3 goes back.
      back-nothing-pin-P3, back-nothing-pin-P3-copy
    (The parenthesis copied whole, "motor M1 (with transistor Q1 M1 P1)", does build: add-motor-paren-copied.)

M4. "stepper motor" and "servo motor" set the kind to motor, and "transistor Q1 M1 P1" gets a DC motor added, drawn
    switched on and off by one NPN -- not a stepper or servo circuit (both are in NOTYET). add-stepper, add-servo.
    (A declared "motor M1" draws the same, as before.)

M5. Unchanged by afea882, but still naming the guide's relay where the question has none (the brief's MEDIUM):
      the diode line's "name the coil: diode D1 K1" in a lamp or buzzer question (back-diode-lamp, back-diode-buzzer);
      the correction turn re-sends the guide with "transistor Q1 K1 P1" under a motor question (fix-motor-guide-K1).
      (In a motor question the NOTYET line's "transistor Q1 K1 P1", copied, now builds right through the free-load
      reading: back-mosfet-copy-npn-line agrees.)

LOW (10)
  - free-LED1-tag, free-LDR1-tag: Q1's unknown names an LED or a sensor by its letters, and is read as the free motor
    (the LDR of "when it gets dark" is then lost without a word but the change note).
  - add-led-question-motor-mention: an LED question that names "the motor controller"; M1 on Q1's line adds a motor,
    the LED left always on.
  - free-diode-also-K1: the guide's K1 on the diode's line too is not read as the same M1; it goes back asking for
    diode D1 M1 (one more round, nothing wrong drawn).
  - free-pin-line-takes-motor: "pin P2 "D10" M1" -- M1 is given to Q1 on P1 all the same; P2's line handed back then
    names Q1 again.
  - back-diode-led, back-mosfet-npn-line-names-K1: K1 named in an LED / motor question (as before).
  - guard rows 1.24.31_2b, 1245_2b, 1246_2b (the 2B's copies of the guide's button example in the relay question):
    the spare pin's line is now only "transistor Q1 K1 Pn", Q1 already switching K1 from the other pin.
